Photograph: Anadolu/Getty Images Indonesia ‘Like a miracle’: 84-year-old woman pulled alive from rubble three days after Indonesian quake A landslide triggered by the quake had blocked access to the village where Paulina Pobi had lived, leaving her buried under the collapsed remains Kate Lamb and agencies Wed 19 Aug 2026 20.57 EDT Last modified on Wed 19 Aug 2026 23.20 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google An 84-year-old woman has been discovered alive in the flattened remains of her home three days after a powerful earthquake hit eastern Indonesia , authorities have confirmed. The 7.7-magnitude quake struck off Indonesia’s Flores island on Saturday morning, killing at least 73 people, injuring more than 900 people and displacing nearly 60,000 others. A landslide triggered by the quake had blocked access to Nitunglea village where Paulina Pobi, 84, lived, leaving the elderly woman buried for three days under the collapsed bamboo walls of her home until Tuesday. Rescue teams search for survivors in Indonesia after powerful earthquake Read more Sikka regency police Bambang Supeno told local media the woman had now been safely evacuated and taken to the nearest health centre for treatment. “Because she was paralysed, she couldn’t move or speak, so it wasn’t until the fourth day that her family finally found her,” another local official, Rudolfus Riba, told Agence France-Presse. “She is in good health; there were no injuries at all. She was just a bit weak because she hadn’t eaten or drunk anything for days.” “It feels unreal, almost like a miracle.” View image in fullscreen Rescuers inspect the ruins of a mosque that collapsed during an earthquake in North Lamba Leda, East Nusa Tenggara province, Indonesia. Photograph: Firdia Lisnawati/AP Grocery stores, petrol stations and other shops have begun to reopen on the island, but debris still covers streets and searchers continue to dig in the rubble for possible victims . Indonesia’s disaster mitigation agency said 398 tons of aid, including food, tents, refugee shelters and donations from the public, have been transported to affected communities. But the distribution process has been slowed by Flores’ mountainous terrain and roads damaged by the shallow quake. The government has expanded the use of military aircraft, ships and personnel to support emergency operations in the remote areas, disaster agency spokesperson Berton Panjaitan said in a video statement. More than 3,000 aftershocks have been recorded since Saturday, at least 86 of them strong enough to be felt by residents, according to Indonesia’s geological agency. The tremors have made many too afraid to return to their damaged homes. Regional police chief inspector general Rudi Darmoko said displaced communities were traumatised by the disaster. “These refugees are not only physically injured, but they also have mental health issues that we must not ignore, especially for children,” he said. Indonesia frequently experiences earthquakes because it lies on the Pacific “Ring of Fire”, a zone of intense seismic and volcanic activity that stretches from Japan through South-east Asia and across the Pacific Ocean. In 2004, a powerful 9.1-magnitude earthquake off the coast of Sumatra triggered a tsunami that killed about 220,000 people across the region, including about 170,000 in Indonesia. https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/defe.text: Poland has joined an anti-ballistic missile coalition with Ukraine and other allies, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said on Friday, as Kyiv seeks to strengthen its air defences against Russian attacks.âFrom today, Poland is part of this major project ... we agreed on the forms and frameworks of this cooperation,â Tusk said in a video posted on X.Tusk made the announcement during a summit of eight Carpathian countries being held in western Ukraine and launched by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.Poland backs joint missile defence projectUkraine and nine European countries announced an air-defence coalition in July that would include the joint development of a new anti-ballistic missile system. The proposed system is intended to provide an alternative and cheaper solution to the US Patriot system.Tusk also said Poland had prepared a new âsignificantâ donation package for Ukraine, although he did not provide details.âI will be very consistent here. No one will change my opinion that Poland has to support Ukraine in its war against Russian aggression ... History cannot divide us vis-a-vis Russia today,â Tusk said.Following a bilateral meeting with Tusk at the summit, Zelenskyy thanked Poland for the new aid package.âUkraine and Poland are strong neighbors, friends, and partners, and we have one common enemy,â he said on social media.Carpathian summit focuses on security, cooperationThe announcement came during the first Carpathian Summit in western Ukraine, which brought together Ukraine, Romania, Serbia, Poland, Slovakia, the Czech Republic, Austria and Hungary, with the European Union also involved.Zelenskyy said the meeting would focus on security, energy, logistics, cross-border economic ties and support for local communities.Business representatives were also expected to participate in discussions on economic cooperation, security and logistics, as Russia targets Ukraine's transport routes, according to news agency AFP.âThe Carpathian macro-region has become one of the most reliable foundations of our defense. This is about strength that exists and will continue to exist,â Zelenskyy said.The summit comes as Ukraine seeks additional missile defence systems to counter Russian ballistic attacks, while also developing interceptors to tackle Russian jet-powered drones.Tusk had said before travelling to Ukraine that âDifficult weeks and months lie ahead for all of us, not just Ukraine. And it's worth showing solidarity at a time like this.âThe meeting was held in the western Ukrainian ski resort of Bukovel amid growing concern among European countries over Russian hybrid threats, including sabotage, cyberattacks, disinformation and potential drone incursions into Nato territory.

Photograph: Houston Chronicle/Hearst Newspapers/Getty Images Texas Texas kills man in first US execution since botched lethal injection of Christa Pike Jamaal Howard, 46, executed by fatal dose of pentobarbital after lawyers’ bid for stay had been denied Uwa Ede-Osifo Wed 7 Oct 2026 21.32 EDT First published on Wed 7 Oct 2026 16.58 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A Texas man was put to death Wednesday in the first US execution since the botched lethal injection of Christa Pike in Tennessee last week. Jamaal Howard, 46, was pronounced dead at 8.03pm after receiving a fatal dose of pentobarbital, a sedative, at the state prison in Huntsville. Howard’s lawyers sought to halt the execution, arguing to the Texas court of criminal appeals there were similar risks of executing Howard using the same lethal injection drug that was used on Pike. Pike survived two doses of pentobarbital and had complained her arms felt like they were going to explode as she was given the drug. “Texas should not be eager to follow in Tennessee’s footsteps,” Howard’s attorneys argued. The court denied the request for a stay and later denied a second attempt to stop the execution over the drug. The court denied both without elaboration. The US supreme court also denied a late appeal Wednesday evening without comment. Judge orders officials to preserve all evidence tied to Christa Pike’s botched execution Read more Texas has executed six people so far this year, with two more lethal injections scheduled after Howard. He is the 30th person executed nationwide in 2026. Howard was found guilty of capital murder in 2001 for robbing a convenience store in Silsbee, a town north of Beaumont, and fatally shooting 42-year-old clerk Vickie Swartout. Asked by the warden if he had a final statement, Howard apologized profusely to members of his victim’s family, who watched through a viewing window just feet from the death chamber. “I wish that you accept my apology and I wish for your forgiveness,” he said, shortly before the injection got underway. “I’m sorry for what happened. I wish you can learn to forgive me one of these days.” His legal team argued that, at the time of the crime, Howard was intellectually disabled and thus ineligible for the death penalty, as the supreme court ruled in 2002. View image in fullscreen Jamaal Howard in this Texas department of criminal justice handout. Photograph: Texas department of criminal justice/AP Pike regained consciousness on Tuesday. Her lawyers say she has pneumonia and is unable to move her arms. Pike’s was the second botched execution in Tennessee this year, and governor Bill Lee has barred any further lethal injections for the rest of the year. He has also ordered a probe into why Pike’s execution failed. Pike’s lawyers had previously argued her blood disorder would make a lethal injection painful. Speculation has also swirled over the quality of the pentobarbital. “There is a similar risk,” Howard’s attorneys wrote in the Wednesday motion filed with Texas’s court of criminal appeals, “that Texas’s execution drugs are likewise degraded, as they are far past the original beyond-use dates that the pharmacopeia allows for drugs of this kind.” Last week, the fifth circuit court of appeals declined a request to stop Howard’s execution. Texas officials did not immediately return a request for comment on Wednesday morning.
